info.title: OpenAsy Network IDS API
info.summary: Suricata alerts, flows and protocol logs from sensors on a copy of your traffic, with local rules and suppressions.
info.description:
Every screen of Network IDS uses this API, and so can your scripts (ADR 0014). Within `/api/v1` changes are additive only; anything removed is deprecated first (ADR 0024). Errors use Problem Details (RFC 9457).

Sensors send their events through network-ids-agent, which enrols once with a token from `POST /api/v1/sensors` and then calls `/api/v1/agent/*` with its own secret. Everything else takes the session of a signed-in person or an API token, and each operation names the role it needs (`x-openasy-role`: viewer, editor, admin; ADR 0003).

Sign-in, members and API tokens are under `/api/v1/auth`, provided by [@openasy/auth](https://github.com/openasy/auth#routes).

session.name: __Host-openasy-session
session.description: The browser session after signing in (`openasy-session` when Network IDS runs on plain http://localhost). Requests that change something must come from the Network IDS origin.

apiToken.description: An API token created under Settings → API tokens (`oa_network-ids_...`): one role, always an expiry (ADR 0003).

adminToken.description: Only when Network IDS is started by its tests or a local script: one shared token with the admin role. A production install does not have it.

agentSecret.description: The secret network-ids-agent got when it enrolled (`oia_...`). It reads the sensor's rules and sends its events, nothing else.

Problem.description: An error, as RFC 9457 Problem Details.

id.description: The product, as OpenAsy names it.

url.description: The address people open it at.

flowId.description: Suricata's flow id on that sensor; the flow and protocol logs of the alert share it.

communityId.description: The Community ID of the flow, when Suricata writes it: the same flow in Zeek and other tools.

severity.description: From ET's signature_severity metadata, or Suricata's severity: 1 high, 2 medium, 3 and more low.

action.description: What Suricata did: allowed, as an IDS does.

suppressedBy.description: The suppression that covers it; such alerts are kept and left out of counts.

total.description: All that match; at most 500 are listed, newest first.

event.description: The EVE event as the sensor sent it, without packet payloads.

state.description: How Suricata saw it end: new, established, closed, bypassed.

reason.description: Why the flow record was written: timeout, forced, shutdown.

bytes.description: Both ways, of every flow that matches.

unanswered.description: Flows the other side sent nothing back on.

longLived.description: Flows of more than an hour: check those for beacons.

name.description: The DNS name, the HTTP host, the TLS server name or the SSH client.

detail.description: The fields kept of Suricata's record: rrtype and rcode, url and user agent, version, subject and JA3.

hash.description: Of the enabled local rules and active suppressions: what an up-to-date sensor wrote.

outdated.description: Enrolled sensors that have not written the current rules and suppressions.

text.description: One rule: alert or pass, a header and options with a msg in quotes and a sid from 9000000 to 9999999. lua, luajit, dataset and datarep are refused.
examples: alert http $EXTERNAL_NET any -> $HOME_NET any (msg:"LOCAL Admin path probe"; http.uri; content:"/admin"; sid:9000104; rev:1;)

line.description: As written in the sensors' threshold file.
examples: suppress gen_id 1, sig_id 2013028, track by_src, ip 192.0.2.9

signature.description: The signature, from the last alert of that sid.

track.description: With network: only alerts from (by_src) or to (by_dst) it.

network.description: An address or a network in CIDR form.

expiresAt.description: Within a year; null for no end.

status.description: degraded: it drops 1% of packets or more, Suricata failed to load rules, or the agent could not write them.

dropRatio.description: 0 to 1, over the last minute of counters.

enrollToken.description: One-time, for 7 days: start network-ids-agent with it. Shown once.

version.description: The agent's version; it must be Network IDS's (ADR 0019).

configHash.description: The hash of the rules and suppressions the agent last wrote.

configError.description: Why the last write or reload failed.

secret.description: The agent's own secret from now on. Shown once.

rules.description: The enabled local rules, one per line of the agent's rules file.

suppressions.description: Suricata suppress lines, for the agent's threshold file.

events.description: EVE events as Suricata wrote them: alert, flow, dns, http, tls, ssh, stats.

ignored.description: Other event types, and events past retention.

duplicate.description: Events already kept: a batch sent again.
